task: Direct three-class EF-based functional classification using the frozen Phase 2 predicted EF.
method: CAMUS reference EF was converted to the frozen Phase 3A EF bands and compared with the class obtained by applying the identical fixed bands to the frozen Phase 2 predicted EF. No classifier was trained.
terminology_note: These labels represent EF-based functional bands for an assistive, non-diagnostic research system and are not standalone heart-failure diagnoses.

boundary_analysis.interpretation: Misclassified patients were descriptively closer to the nearest 40% or 50% EF boundary, but the difference was not statistically significant in this 50-patient evaluation sample. Boundary proximity alone therefore did not explain all classification errors.

patient0217.interpretation: The dominant disagreement occurred before segmentation propagation: even GT-mask geometry produced an EF far above the CAMUS reference EF. The segmentation-derived EF was slightly lower than GT geometry. This case is therefore primarily a reference-versus-geometric-method disagreement rather than a segmentation-driven classification failure.

patient0072.interpretation: Both reference-versus-geometry disagreement and segmentation propagation contributed to the final two-class transition.

main_findings: The direct frozen quantitative pipeline achieved 66.0% exact three-class agreement with the reference EF-based functional bands.
Higher EF showed the highest recall at 90.0%, while Intermediate EF was the most difficult class with 35.7% recall and F1 of 0.400.
Fifteen of seventeen classification errors (88.24%) were adjacent-band errors.
Twelve of seventeen misclassified patients were assigned to a higher EF band than their reference band.
Boundary proximity alone did not adequately explain classification disagreement.
The two largest class-jump errors had different error sources, demonstrating that end-to-end classification failure cannot be attributed solely to segmentation.
limitations: The Intermediate EF band spans a relatively narrow range and is sensitive to quantitative EF disagreement.
Predicted EF inherits both segmentation error and single-plane geometry/reference-method disagreement.
The evaluation partition had historical pilot exposure and is not described as a pristine external test set.
